extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting to Royal Society journals (also relevant to reviewers and editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and publisher policies authors must follow to support open science when submitting to Royal Society journals, covering data/code sharing, peer review openness, authorship credit, preprints, registered reports and replication submissions. Useful for authors, reviewers and editors implementing or evaluating these practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data (condition of publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a condition of publication that authors make available the data, code and research materials supporting the results in the article with an open license (CC0 or CC-BY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information on the open data policy is available via the journal’s open data policy and can be cited by DOI via FAIRsharing.org. This requirement aims to allow others to verify and build on published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material licensing and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: All supplementary material (including video) is published under a CC-BY licence alongside the paper on the journal website and deposited on Figshare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content on this dedicated channel is fully searchable and citable; supplementary materials are therefore openly licensed and archived in a public repository to enhance discoverability and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article and journal metrics (DORA adherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Publishing is a signatory to DORA (San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment) which challenges the impact factor as the main means for evaluating science and promotes assessing research on its own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To move focus away from journal impact factor, the publisher offers a variety of journal and article-based metrics to evaluate article 'success' more appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open citations (I4OC membership and open reference lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher is a member of the Initiative for Open Citations (I4OC) and has made all references in published articles openly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open citation data promotes an unrestricted scholarly citation web, enhancing discoverability of published content and particularly benefiting individuals without access to commercial citation databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints are permitted and encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher encourages researchers to deposit pre-publication versions of articles in appropriate preprint repositories and does not consider posting of preprints to be 'prior publication'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports rapid communication and increased accessibility of research; authors may share preprints without jeopardising later submission to Royal Society journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and contributions (CRediT)
rubrics_metrics.description: All published articles contain an Authors’ Contributions section which lists the specific contribution of each author in the published article, implemented through the machine-readable CRediT taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide specific role attributions (e.g., conceptualization, data curation, writing) so contribution statements are transparent and structured for machine-readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals operate open peer review by making reviewer reports, decision letters and associated author responses accessible alongside published articles; referee reports are made public under an open access licence (CC-BY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented via Web of Science Transparent Peer Review for specified journals (e.g., Royal Society Open Science, Open Biology, Proceedings A and B). Transparency entails publishing the review history with the article to make the review process as open as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective peer review (soundness-only review option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Open Science publishes research on the basis of objective peer review: it accepts all articles which are scientifically sound and useful to the community without assessing novelty or potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective peer review allows consideration and publication of negative or null results and evaluates methodological/scientific soundness and usefulness rather than novelty or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports (two-stage pre-registration and review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Registered Report is a journal article in which methods and proposed analyses are pre-registered and peer-reviewed prior to research being conducted (stage 1). High-quality protocols can be provisionally accepted for publication before data collection; stage 2 completes the article with results and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the final study conforms to the initially approved proposal and meets quality checks, publication is virtually guaranteed: the journal commits to publishing results regardless of outcome, reducing publication bias. Peer review at stage 1 helps authors refine study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication studies (inviting and publishing valid replications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher invites submission of replications of previous studies and has a Replication Policy committing to publishing valid replications of studies previously published in the Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience section or in other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing empirical studies the journal assumes responsibility for replicability and welcomes replication submissions to reflect that responsibility; replication validity is the basis for publication under this policy.
